Subject: Azure PO: invoice routing + distributor cut?

Hi Tessa,

Quick question as we prepare procurement paperwork for the Azure private offer: how does Redwood expect invoice routing to work when a distributor is in the middle? Our procurement team needs to know whether the distributor will invoice CloudMed (our reseller) directly, or whether Azure invoices CloudMed and then the distributor handles a reconciliation/credit. Specifically we need:

- The invoice "handshake" flow (who receives the Marketplace invoice).
- How the distributor cut will be represented (line item vs. off-invoice credit).
- Any evidence Redwood needs to support the distributor fee during our internal procurement audit.

We have a target go-live on 1 Jul; if you can provide a short summary and any sample term sheet language it would be ideal.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Azure PO: invoice routing + distributor cut?

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Ben (finance/marketplace billing) and Irene (marketplace ops) so we can give a consolidated answer.

Short answer (overview):
- Azure issues the initial marketplace invoice to CloudMed (the buyer) as the transacting party unless the private offer is configured for distributor billing.
- Distributor fees can be implemented two ways: (1) visible line item on your invoice (if the distributor is the transacting party) or (2) off-invoice settlement where Redwood invoices the distributor separately and the distributor provides a credit/commission to CloudMed.

We need a few quick datapoints from you to recommend the cleanest path and to populate procurement docs:
1) Will CloudMed insist on a single invoice from Azure (no distributor invoice accepted)?
2) Expected first-month spend estimate (USD) and monthly ramp.
3) Distributor entity name and billing relationship (if already confirmed).

Action items:
- Ben will propose the invoice path and show a simple waterfall that preserves your distributor margin line.
- Irene will confirm operational limitations in Azure Private Offer config (what we can surface on the invoice vs. what must be off-invoice).
- I will draft term-sheet text and attach a PDF (v1) with the suggested fields for procurement.

If you can share the three datapoints above by EOD Monday we’ll get a draft term sheet and the workback back to you.

Best,

> Short answer (overview):
> - Azure issues the initial marketplace invoice to CloudMed (the buyer) as the transacting party unless the private offer is configured for distributor billing.

Hi all — quick finance note and proposed workback attached. Key points from finance perspective:

- If CloudMed requires a single consolidated invoice from Azure, the distributor fee typically needs to be implemented as an off-invoice commission (we invoice the distributor, they remit to the reseller).
- If the distributor is configured as the transacting party, their cut will appear as a separate line item on the Azure invoice; that is simplest for reconciliation but requires the distributor to be in the transacting role in the private offer setup.

Proposed waterfall (attached):
1) Gross marketplace charge (Azure line)
2) Distributor cut (either visible line or off-invoice settlement)
3) Redwood net (what we recognize after distributor brokerage)

Attachment: az_po_commission_workback.xlsx (simple example with a $120k first-month and 15% distributor cut).

If CloudMed confirms they need Azure-only invoicing, we’ll push the off-invoice flow and provide evidence (billing memos, commission agreement) for procurement.

– Ben
